What is AI

The building blocks of
artificial intelligence

AI encompasses a wide range of technologies that enable machines to mimic human intelligence, from learning and reasoning to perception and creativity.

Machine Learning

Algorithms that learn from data, identifying patterns and making decisions with minimal human intervention.

Computer Vision

Enabling machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world around them.

Generative AI

Creating new content — text, images, code, and music — that rivals human creativity.

Neural Networks

Deep architectures inspired by the human brain, processing information through layers of interconnected nodes.

AI Safety

Ensuring artificial intelligence systems are developed and deployed responsibly for the benefit of humanity.

Real-Time Processing

Lightning-fast inference engines powering applications from autonomous vehicles to live translation.

The Journey

A brief history of artificial intelligence

1950

The Turing Test

Alan Turing proposes the imitation game, laying the philosophical groundwork for artificial intelligence.

1956

Dartmouth Conference

The term 'artificial intelligence' is coined at a summer workshop at Dartmouth College.

1997

Deep Blue vs Kasparov

IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov, a landmark moment for AI.

2012

Deep Learning Revolution

AlexNet wins ImageNet, proving deep neural networks can dramatically outperform traditional methods.

2017

The Transformer

Google publishes 'Attention Is All You Need', introducing the architecture behind modern LLMs.

2022

ChatGPT Era

OpenAI releases ChatGPT, bringing AI to mainstream audiences and changing how we interact with technology.

2025

The Frontier

AI agents, multimodal models, and reasoning systems push the boundaries of what machines can achieve.
